bio.summary: Rendleman is an attorney running for council for the first time. His stated priorities include wildfire preparedness, housing affordability and trust in city government.

statements.text: Yes, I supported sending the Downtown Development Authority proposal to the November ballot.
statements.speaker: Scott Rendleman

statements.text: I support reconsideration of the DDA.
statements.speaker: Scott Rendleman
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Scott Rendleman

statements.text: According to Rendleman, he was disappointed that the DDA didn’t go forward this year – it lost on a 4-4 Council tie – and he would have voted for it had he been on Council at the time.
statements.speaker: Richard Valenty reporting Scott Rendleman’s interview

statements.text: City government currently appears focused on managing growth and housing, advancing climate goals, and addressing public safety and homelessness.
statements.speaker: Scott Rendleman

statements.text: So much of the Boulder community feels that City Council is not listening to its concerns, and it's one of the reasons I'm running this year.
statements.speaker: Scott Rendleman
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Scott Rendleman

statements.text: Rendleman stated that he did not at first appreciate the high-rises being built in Boulder, but currently favors more development rather than sprawl.
statements.speaker: Peter Constas (reporting the candidate)

statements.text: Scott Rendleman is a first-time candidate for Boulder City Council running on a platform of climate resilience, particularly wildfire preparedness, stronger trust in government and more affordable housing.
statements.speaker: Boulder Reporting Lab reporter

statements.text: Yes. Ordinance 8666 was a modest, incremental modification of the Land Use Code to allow potential development, within 350 feet of bus routes.
statements.speaker: Scott Rendleman

statements.text: Boulder businesses rightfully expect commercial districts to remain safe and clean.
statements.speaker: Scott Rendleman
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Scott Rendleman

statements.text: No. The CAN has strong city support, but the community does not yet show sufficient backing for this; the Iris plan remains too contentious now.
statements.speaker: Scott Rendleman
